faq.a: Suha is associated with the Arabic form سُهَا, whose core sense is suha; a faint star.

faq.q: What is the origin of Suha?
faq.a: Suha is associated with Arabic. Suha is Arabic سُهَا (Suhā), the name of a faint star in the Big Dipper.
Yes — the underlying form سُهَا is Arabic.
Suha can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Suha, suha. Script forms are سها, سُهَا, سہا, सुहा.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
